title: Inheritance Package
description: Open, human-readable source format for a local-first inheritance plan. A property graph of People, Locations, Items, Guides, Folders and Attachments. Designed to be read by humans (plain JSON) and by any compatible reader app, and to remain understandable for 10+ years with no server, account, or proprietary runtime. By default the package is a MAP of where secrets live and how to combine them; raw secrets are stored only when an item is explicitly marked `sensitive` and carries a `secret` object.

schema.description: Format identifier + version. Lets any future reader recognise and validate the package.

date.description: ISO-8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD). Shown to heirs as 'Last updated'.

importance.description: How critical this is for the heir. Shown as an accessible High/Medium/Low label (not colour alone).

order.description: Optional explicit sort position set by the plan author (lower = earlier). Items without `order` sort after those with one. Lets the owner choose the order people/items/locations/guides appear in.

localizedText.description: A string keyed by language code. Keys must appear in package.languages.

title.description: Human title, e.g. 'Inheritance plan of Person A'.

updated.description: Date of the most recent change to the whole package.

languages.description: All languages used anywhere in this package.

nickname.description: Familiar name shown in lists and guides instead of the legal name, when present.

display_as.description: How the owner addresses them, e.g. 'my wife', 'Dad'.

roles.description: owner = plan author. primary_heir = the person who drives everything. helper = supports, does not act alone. beneficiary = legally inherits. expert/professional = technical or paid help. contact = person to inform. guardian = cares for dependents.

location_id.description: Where this person is based, if relevant.

verification.description: A control question/answer the heir can use to confirm a person's identity (anti-scam).

boundaries.description: Role limits, e.g. 'helper only — never acts alone unless the primary heir is unavailable'.

parent_id.description: Containing location. Arbitrary depth — this is how nesting works.

depends_on_ids.description: Items this location depends on, such as keys, codes, documents or devices needed to access it.

secret.description: A raw secret value. Present ONLY when the owner deliberately chose to store it (the item must also be sensitive=true). Best practice is to keep these out of the package and store a pointer instead.

item.description: An asset, credential, device, document or piece of infrastructure. `properties` is a free-form, type-specific bag so different item types can carry different fields.

location_ids.description: Where it lives. Multiple = redundant copies (e.g. duplicated across countries).

depends_on_ids.description: Other items this one needs (e.g. an account depends on the SIM for 2FA; a multisig wallet depends on its seeds). Powers single-point-of-failure / circular-dependency checks.

guide_ids.description: Guides that explain how to use / recover this item.

sensitive.description: If true, this item may contain a raw secret and should be visually flagged + handled with extra care.

properties.description: Type-specific fields, e.g. {login, url, price, notes} for a password_record; {wallet_role, device, checksum} for a btc_seed; {value, access, next_steps} for an account_investment.

guide.description: Human-readable instructions. Content is Markdown, keyed per language. Print-type guides render to the /print folder.

group.description: Optional single menu group/category for this guide, e.g. 'bitcoin'. Guides with the same group are displayed together.

content.description: Markdown body keyed by language code.

references.description: Cross-links this guide makes, so a reader can render clickable references and detect dangling links.

is_print.description: True for the special PRINT group (artifacts meant to be printed).

attachment.description: An original file (image, PDF...) shipped alongside the package and referenced by relative path.

path.description: Relative path within the package, e.g. 'attachments/bitcoin/multisig_descriptor.png'.
